newsitem.title: UK: FROM THE FLIGHTDECK - The Air Cargo Week In Review.
newsitem.headline: FROM THE FLIGHTDECK - The Air Cargo Week In Review.

text.p: This is Reuters' look back at the major development in the air cargo industry in the week November 1 to November 8th.
**NOVEMBER 1**
LONDON - British trucking companies which service the air cargo industry are imposing five percent fuel surcharges from November 1 to counter the impact of higher diesel fuel costs.
SINGAPORE - Freight Links Express Holdings have entered into a conditional agreement to buy 8.15 million shares in Caxton Holdings for A$5.5 million from Eftus Investments Pty Ltd.
MOSCOW - Russia AO Aviastar aircraft manufacturer to resume work Nov 3 after 10-week stoppage caused by financial problems.
PARIS - Air France is considering increasing passenger fares on flights from France from November 4, but new rates yet to be finalised.
ZURICH - Swissair cutting fares to 32 destinations in 18 mainly European countries, for flights between November 8 and December 8 by around 50 percent.
LONDON - MSAS has appointed Teresa Vitch as managing director of its Spanish operating company.
*MSAS gains ISO 9002 award for all forwarding services from Madrid.
CALGARY - Canadian Airlines Corp said its Canadian International unit had Q3 net income of C$85.7 million bringing losses for first nine months of 1996 to a worse than planned C$49 million
*CAL, struggling for survival amind heavy losses says it would transfer capacity, seek wage cuts from employees and ask for concessions from U.S. shareholder American Airlines.
FORTH WORTH - American Airlines remains committed to its stake in Canadian Airlines but does not plan any further investment in the ailing carrier.
LONDON, European jet prices tumbled on back of falling IPE gas oil, futures.
HONG KONG - Asiana airlines is increasing its ex-Seoul cargo rates by five percent from November 1 because of peak season demand and higher fuel prices.
AMSTERDAM - The Dutch ministry of transport is investigating an incident where an El Al freighter flew just 260 metres over Amsterdam.
WASHINGTON - Strong demand for commerical aircraft drove new orders to U.S. factories higher during September.
CALGARY - Canadian Airlines, struggling to survive amid heavy losses, plans to increase flights to the U.S., negotiate wage cuts and seek concessions from U.S. shareholders AMR Corp.
OTTAWA - Canadian transport minister welcomes Canadian Airlines tought measures to control costs.
HONG KONG - El Al to use 747 in place of 767 on Tel Aviv/Hkg route to increase cargo capacity and tourism.
SAO PAULO - Federal investigation begins into cause of Fokker-100 crash which killed at least 104 people on Nov 1.
LONDON - European airlines led the way in introducing 10 US cent a kg cargo fuel surcharge.
FORT WORTH - American Air's Oct load factor up 2.9 percent to 69.0 percent.

AMSTERDAM - Dutch government optimistic on Samsung Aerospace's rescue package for Dutch Fokker planemaker. Earlier major suppliers indicated they were willing to wait a few more days for a poossible rescue.
LOS ANGELES - Boeing Co shares fell three points to 92-3/8 after it said development of next generation of 747s could cost as much as $7 billion.
NEW YORK -USAir rated strong buy by Salomon Brother after cutting costs.
CALGARY - Canadian Airlines' biggest union rejects carrier's survival plan based on lower wages.
FORT WORTH - American Airlines to implement 10 cent/kg fuel surcharge effective Nov 15 on most routes.
SEATTLE - Boeing recommends tests of rudder power controls on its 737s.
NEW YORK - U.S. airlines face minimal costs to comply with safety changes needed for Boeing 737s.
DALLAS - Southwest Airlines cuts 7-day advance purchase fares for many flights Dec 3 to April 4, 1997.
**November 2**
MANILA - Phillipine Airlines ground crew end three-day strike returning to work Sunday.
LONDON - BA checking over next few days on Boeing 737 rudder systems.
**November 3**
TAIPEI - A Taiwan cabinet panel has proposed building a T$10 billion airport town in northern county of Taoyuan.
GENEVA - New directions for air industry expected to be under discussion at this week's IATA AGM here.
ZURICH - Swissair chief says will not abandon Belgian partner carrier Sabena.
SEATTLE - Boeing may ask airlines to install rudder limiterson its 737s.
**November 4**
SYDNEY - Qantas had 37.7 percent of international passenger market in and out of Australia for year to end-July.
*Qantas completes checks on 737s without finding faults.
*Australian airlines Qantas and Ansett have no plans to impose fuel surcharge on cargo or passenger fares.
HONG KONG- Macau International airport said both passenger and cargo traffic in October set new records.

TORONTO - Canadian Airlines fuel surcharges of C12 cents/kg on international flights and C5cents/kg on domestic ones effective Nov 25. Air Canada expected to start westbound North Atlantic surcharges Nov 15 equivalent to US$0.10/kg.
DUBAI - Emirates airline said it is to buy 16 Airbus A330-200s with option for 7 more replacing A310 and A300 from 1999 to 2002.
*Dubai airport cargo volumes rose 13 percent in October to 32,082 tonnes from 28,314 tonnes in the same month last year, Dubai Cargo Village figures show.
*Lufthansa's Oct quality report for cargo handling at Sharjah show handling targets mainly met.
GENEVA - IATA head says airlines soaring fuel bills eating into airlines revenues but profits still heading for second successive record year.
*Air Transport Action Group (ATAG) said world industry employed 24 million in 1994 or 2 million more than in 1992.
*IATA said at AGM it would launch judicial challenge to new British law on lower noise limits for aircraft taking off from London airports from Jan one.
*Lufthansa and Swissair plan to lift passenger airfares due to rising fuel costs, following earlier increases for air cargo, top executives told a news conference but set no date for the increase.
*American Airlines chairman said its fuel bills so far this year have risen $300-400 million because of high jet fuel prices.
*American Airlines chief said expects regulatory approval for its tie-up with BA by end-March 1997.
VIENNA - Tyrolean Airways raising prices by average three percent effective Nov 4 because of fuel costs.
JOHANNESBURG - SAS introducing air cargo surcharge from S Africa of 0.50 rand/kg effective Nov 15 and of US$0.10/kg ex-S Africa.
RABAT - Morocco's Royal Air Maroc ordered two Boeing 737-800s for April 1998 delivery.

AMSTERDAM - Nippon Cargo Airline, the Japanese all-cargo airline, is likely to implement a fuel surcharge from the Netherlands shortly, said Gino Laan, an Amsterdam based NCA marketing executive ....ISTANBUL - Shares representing 15 percent capital of Turkish airport ground handling firm Celebi Hava Servisi will be offered to the public on November 7-8.
LONDON - Rolls Royce signs MOU with Airbus consortium specifying its Trent 900 as engine for the planned new A3XX large capacity airliner.
ATLANTA - ValuJet realigns management structure and names D Joseph Carr president and chief executive from Nov 6.
NEW YORK - Gulfstream listed as strong buy by Morgan Stanley and recommended by Goldman Sachs.
PARIS, Nov 4 (Reuter) - France's association of air freight forwarding agents, SNAGFA, said the way surcharges on freight had been applied, to cover rising jet fuel costs, was totally "unacceptable.
*Air France imposes surcharge because of fuel costs.
MAASTRICHT - Dutch Cabinet approves limited expansion of the country's most southerly airport, a Ministry of Transport spokesman said.
NEW YORK - Federal Express shares rally on news it will add 20 Chinese cities a year to delivery area over next five years.
*Investigators seeking the cause of the TWA Flight 800 disaster begin dredging part of the crash site.
CALGARY - Analysts said Canadian Airlines rescue plan falls short of addressing the cash drain caused by domestic overcapacity.
MEXICO CITY - Two Mexican states are trying to convince the federal government where to locate a second airport for Mexico City.
ZURICH - Global cargo traffic handled at Zurich Jan-Sept totalled 325,482 tonnes, down 0.9 percent on the same period last year, airport authority figures show.
*Swissair shipments in Jan-Sept rose six pct to 1.2 billion freight tonnes kilometres with most growth to the Far East and South Atlantic.
*Swissair said Sept cargo traffic rose eight pct from Sept last year to 136.1 million freight tonne kilometres.
PARIS - French TAT airline union representing attendents calls one day strike for Nov 5 in protest at staffing levels.
*RIGA - Latvia wants talks on its dispute with Russia over flying rights between the two coubntries.
MOSCOW - Lufthansa has begun operating A319-100 airliners on its regular routes to medium-range Russian and CIS destinations.
TORONTO - Major US carriers slow to match American Airlines' plans for fuel surcharges on international cargo routes.
MIAMI - Some Latam airlines resist fuel surcharges on cargo although many have put surcharges on.
AMSTERDAM - Varig will put an as yet unspecified surcharge on cargo ex-Netherlands but this is likely to be in line with other increases.
*Korea Airways announced ex-Amsterdam fuel surcharge of 10 US cents/kg from Nov 15.
ZOETERMEET, the Netherlands - Dutch shippers have called for a detailed breakdown of KLM's recent air carg fuel surcharge.
BRUSSELS - AEA Sept figures show major European airlines carried six pct more passengers in Sept than year ago, but N America lower.
*AEA Jan-Sept traffic higher on most routes except for intra-European ones.
WASHINGTON - US Transportation Dept lists punctuality and complaints for domestic US flights in Sept.
